content.thinking: I should fix the wording issues: swap "logged from" for "logged over," replace "half hour before" with something like "in the stretch before the onset," and change "within about a minute" to "almost at once."

action_items.item: Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so the account page handles a zero divisor, before monthly-spend-feature is switched on again.
Add a test that renders the account page with monthly-spend-feature on and covers the case that hit the division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.
Roll out io-shop flag changes, monthly-spend-feature included, in stages, with an error-rate check that halts the rollout and reverts the flag when errors rise.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call paging rotation.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The service's share of failed requests rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} while it was broken, and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The account page error rate was highest at {Gbac1.7}.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors were logged over {G5309.3} and not before the onset.

From the onset, monthly-spend-feature evaluated on for most requests and then for all of them, which sent account page requests down the code path that holds that division. Over {G7e5d.4} every evaluation was off. At {G971b.6} it was off {G971b.1} and on {G971b.2}, and over {Gce95.4} every evaluation was on.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release: the change query for the day before the onset returned only the flag toggle and no deploys, and all replicas run a single revision.
Shoppers disconnecting: ClientDisconnected errors were logged over {G46bc.3}, while account pages were still rendering normally, and none were logged after the onset.

causal_chain.step: The flag was on because admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. The flag provider's history shows this as the one flag change by anyone but Argus in the window it read.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly-spend feature made the account page run a calculation that divided by zero, so those pages failed to load.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag change reached all account page traffic almost at once. No staged rollout and no error-rate check that halts a flag change were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout with an automatic halt would have kept the failure to a small share of shoppers and switched the flag back as soon as errors rose.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test or pre-production check was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on, which could have caught the division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 before the flag went on in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before shoppers reached it, and the flag would not have been switched on until it was fixed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged when it fired.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An on-call engineer would have been engaged as soon as the alert fired, rather than depending on someone happening to watch the Argus UI.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well: The error logs named the exact file and line of the failure, src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, which tied the failure straight to the newly enabled code path.
The Investigator named the flag toggle as the leading candidate {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and that change can be undone.

input.root_cause: Switching monthly-spend-feature on sent account page requests down a code path that divides by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. Those requests raised ZeroDivisionError and failed instead of rendering. The record does not show why the divisor was zero.
input.still_at_risk: The code that divides by zero is still behind monthly-spend-feature, so switching the flag back on could make account pages fail again.
input.symptom: Account pages failed to load for many shoppers
